assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Neuron
items.clue: A cell of the nervous system that carries electrical impulses.

items.label: Transmembrane receptor
items.clue: A protein in the postsynaptic membrane to which a neurotransmitter binds.

items.label: Synaptic cleft
items.clue: The narrow fluid-filled gap, about 20 nm wide, between the presynaptic membrane and the postsynaptic membrane.

items.label: Correlation coefficient (r)
items.clue: A statistic between −1 and +1 that measures the strength and direction of a linear relationship between two variables.

questions.stem: A motor neuron has its cell body in the spinal cord and a single fibre about 1 m long that reaches a muscle in the foot. What is this fibre?

options.text: One of the neuron's several axons, each of which reaches a different muscle in the leg.
An axon: a single long fibre along which impulses are conducted away from the cell body.
A nerve, because a fibre this long must be made of many neurons joined end to end.
A connecting fibre that links the neuron to the muscle but is not part of the neuron itself.

questions.stem: Why is a nerve impulse described as an electrical signal?

options.text: It consists of electrons flowing along the inside of the fibre, in the same way as a current in a metal wire.
It consists of positively charged ions moving across the membrane, which changes the membrane potential.
It consists of neurotransmitter molecules travelling along the fibre and carrying their electrical charge with them.
It consists of sodium ions flowing along the whole length of the fibre from one end of it to the other.

questions.stem: Which statement about a synapse is correct?

options.text: A signal can pass across it in either direction, depending on which of the two neurons is stimulated first.
It is found only where two neurons meet, so muscle fibres are stimulated directly by the nerve impulse.
A signal can pass across it in one direction only, from the presynaptic cell to the postsynaptic cell.
The action potential jumps across the gap as an electrical spark, so no chemical is needed to cross the cleft.

questions.stem: What is the role of calcium ions in the release of neurotransmitter from a presynaptic neuron?

options.text: Depolarization of the presynaptic membrane opens calcium channels; calcium ions enter and signal vesicles to fuse with the membrane.
Calcium ions are released from the presynaptic neuron and diffuse across the cleft, where they then depolarize the postsynaptic membrane.
Calcium ions have no role, because neurotransmitter simply diffuses out through the presynaptic membrane when an impulse arrives.
Calcium ions provide the energy for carrier proteins to pump the neurotransmitter across the synaptic cleft to its postsynaptic receptors.

questions.stem: How does acetylcholine generate an excitatory postsynaptic potential?

options.text: It diffuses across the cleft and enters the postsynaptic cell, where it depolarizes the membrane from the inside.
It is actively transported across the cleft by carrier proteins, which use ATP to push it into the postsynaptic cell.
It diffuses across the cleft and binds to transmembrane receptors, opening channels through which sodium ions enter the postsynaptic cell.
It diffuses across the cleft and binds to receptors, opening channels through which potassium ions enter the postsynaptic cell.

questions.stem: Electrodes inside and outside an axon show that the inside briefly becomes positive relative to the outside as an impulse passes. What causes this change?

options.text: Potassium ions move into the axon across the membrane at that point.
Electrons move out of the axon along the inner surface of its membrane.
Sodium ions move into the axon across the membrane at that point.
Sodium ions arriving from further back along the axon accumulate at that point.

questions.explanation: During an action potential sodium ions diffuse into the axon through the membrane, adding positive charge inside so that the membrane potential briefly reverses to positive. The impulse is electrical because of this movement of positively charged ions.

questions.stem: Why can a signal pass in only one direction across a synapse?

options.text: Electric current can only cross the cleft from the more positive presynaptic membrane to the more negative postsynaptic one.
Calcium ions can only diffuse across the cleft from the presynaptic side, because that is where they are concentrated.
Carrier proteins in the cleft actively transport the neurotransmitter towards the postsynaptic membrane only.
Only the presynaptic neuron stores neurotransmitter in vesicles, and only the postsynaptic membrane has receptors for it.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between a ligand and its receptor?

options.text: The ligand binds reversibly to a binding site on the receptor protein that is complementary to it, and the receptor changes shape.
The receptor's binding site converts the ligand into a product, in the way an enzyme's active site converts a substrate.
Any ligand reaching a cell binds to it, because every cell carries receptors for every signalling chemical in the body.
The ligand passes through a channel in the receptor into the cytoplasm, where it brings about the response directly.

questions.stem: What is quorum sensing in bacteria?

options.text: Bacteria counting neighbouring cells through direct contact between the surface proteins of their cell walls.
Bacteria of one species each responding on their own to the concentration of nutrients in their environment.
Bacteria secreting a chemical that itself gives out light once enough of it has built up around the cells.
A change in gene expression across a population when a secreted signal reaches a threshold concentration.

questions.stem: Which statement about the functional categories of signalling chemicals in animals is correct?

options.text: Cytokines are small proteins, secreted mainly by cells of the immune system, that act mostly on nearby cells.
Calcium ions are secreted by an endocrine gland into the blood and carried to distant target organs.
Cytokines are secreted by endocrine glands into the blood, from which they act on distant organs.
Neurotransmitters are carried in the blood from a neuron to the target cells of distant organs.

questions.stem: To which chemical groups do the hormones epinephrine, insulin and testosterone belong?

options.text: Epinephrine, insulin and testosterone are all proteins made of amino acids.
Epinephrine is a steroid, insulin is a protein and testosterone is a steroid as well.
Epinephrine is an amine, insulin is a protein and testosterone is a steroid.
Epinephrine is an amine, insulin is a protein and testosterone is a small protein.

questions.explanation: These are the three chemical groups of hormones the guide requires: amines derived from an amino acid (epinephrine), proteins (insulin) and steroids derived from cholesterol (testosterone).

questions.stem: What is meant by the initiation of a signal transduction pathway by a receptor?

options.text: The ligand enters the cytoplasm after binding and itself performs the response inside the cell.
The receptor converts the ligand into a product, and the product produced is the cell's response.
The receptor makes exactly one molecule of response product for each ligand molecule that binds to it.
Ligand binding changes the receptor's shape, setting off a sequence of responses in the cell.

questions.stem: How does a G protein-coupled receptor convey a signal into a cell?

options.text: The ligand passes through a channel in the receptor and binds directly to the G protein, which lies in the cytoplasm just beneath the membrane.
The G protein is released from the membrane into the blood as a second messenger that carries the signal to neighbouring cells of the tissue.
Binding of the ligand outside changes the receptor's shape, activating a G protein on the inner face, which then activates an effector.
The activated G protein converts ATP into cAMP directly, and the cAMP then brings about the response inside the cell.
